- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.0) or shows strong downward momentum, model often underestimates; increase forecast lows by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below prior high.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.0–0.5), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast toward historical 30-day average if deviation >3σ.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture early downward trends; add 1–2 lagged negative sentiment days to forecast if sentiment drops below 0.3.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 1.0 → 0.0 → 1.0), model overfits recent highs; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast tail.
